standard_prerequisites.name: Simplicial objects and the complexes N and s
standard_prerequisites.statement: For a simplicial object U of an abelian category, the associated chain complex s(U) with differentials the alternating sums of faces, and the normalised complex N(U) obtained by dividing by degenerate simplices.
standard_prerequisites.use: They are the objects of the statement (source lines 4033-4036).

standard_prerequisites.name: Splitting of the canonical map on each degree
standard_prerequisites.statement: The subobject N(U_n) of U_n has a complement, by the author's splitting lemma and the definition of a split situation (retained as context).
standard_prerequisites.use: It makes D(U)_n a legitimate complement on which the subcomplex claim can be checked (source lines 4052-4054).

standard_prerequisites.name: The simplicial identities
standard_prerequisites.statement: The relations between face and degeneracy maps, used here in the form d^n_i composed with s^{n-1}_j equals a degenerate composite, and the vanishing of the corresponding maps on N.
standard_prerequisites.use: They settle the exceptional case m = n-1 of the induction (source lines 4100-4112).

core_obligations: Define the complement: set D(U)_n to be the image of the sum of the maps N(U_m) to U_n over all surjections [n] to [m] with m < n, and check that it is complementary to N(U_n) (source lines 4045-4055).
Compute the differential on that image: show that the differential of an element of the image is the alternating sum of the maps U(varphi composed with the faces) (source lines 4055-4070).
Run the induction: prove by ascending induction on m that each of those maps carries N(U_m) into D(U)_{n-1}, distinguishing the case where the composite is still surjective (source lines 4070-4100).

Settle the top case and conclude: treat m = n-1 using the simplicial identities and the definition of the normalised complex, so that D(U) is a subcomplex and the decomposition is functorial (source lines 4100-4112).

proof_roadmap.step: Define D(U)_n as the image of the surjection-indexed sum and see it is complementary to N(U_n).
Write the differential of an element of that image as the alternating sum of the face-composed maps.
Prove by ascending induction on m that those maps land in D(U)_{n-1}.
Handle the case m = n-1 with the simplicial identities and conclude.

difficulty_reason: The counted unit is the author's own lemma lemma-decompose-associated-complexes at source lines 4032-4043: for a simplicial object U of an abelian category the canonical morphism N(U) to s(U) is split, indeed s(U) is the direct sum of N(U) and a functorial complement D(U). The proof at source lines 4045-4113 defines D(U)_n as the image of the sum of the maps N(U_m) to U_n over all surjections [n] to [m] with m < n, uses the splitting lemma to see that this is complementary to N(U_n), and then verifies that D(U) is a subcomplex: the differential of an element of that image is a signed sum of maps U(varphi composed with the face maps), and each summand is shown to land in D(U) by ascending induction on m, with the top case m = n-1 handled separately through the simplicial identities between faces and degeneracies and the definition of N. The substance is the induction and the identification of the exceptional case, not the statement.
